newsitem.title: USA: Judge approves Missouri desegregation settlement.
newsitem.headline: Judge approves Missouri desegregation settlement.

text.p: A federal district judge approved a settlement agreement Tuesday that will release Missouri from making court-ordered desegregation payments to the Kansas City School District.

Judge Russell Clark's ruling closes another chapter in the most expensive desegregation effort in U.S. history. Clark ruled that the state's 10-year $1.3 billion expenditure had fulfilled all of its obligations that were part of a 1985 court order.
Under the terms of the settlement, Missouri will pay $105 million for the 1997-98 school year and $99 million for the 1998-99 school year. The state will cease making payments on June 30, 1999.
Missouri Attorney General Jay Nixon, who negotiated the settlement last May with the school board and the Kansas City teachers' federation, praised Clark's ruling.

"The court recognized the unparalleled and unprecedented efforts the state has made to correct injustices of the past and to meet every legal obligation of the desegregation order," Nixon said in a statement.

For the state of Missouri, Clark's ruling caps a legal battle that began with a lawsuit originally filed in 1977. That lawsuit led to a series of court orders that aimed to improve education in the school district and forced the state to pick up some of the costs.
